children: slashed its profit guidance for 2026 as the German automaker reamins plagued by sluggish Chinese sales, headwinds from its underperforming brands, and a goodwill impairment charge related to Porsche AG.
Return on sales is now expected to be just 1% this year, a significant difference from an earlier projection of 4% to 5.5%. Volkswagen
now expects group sales revenue of €315B, the midpoint of its previous range.

attributes much of the €10B in profit erosion to challenges in China and a shift towards battery-electric vehicles (BHEVs), the latter of which is weighing disproportionately on its Audi and Volkswagen Passenger Car divisions.
Updated guidance for its Porsche segment is also requiring parent company Volkswagen
to take a non-cash impairment charge of ~€6B.

The remaining €2B in negative adjustments is a result of early retirement schemes, costs associated with the sale of its Osnabruck GmbH facility, and non-cash asset impairments with its Chinese joint ventures.
Despite the negative impacts to 2026 guidance, Volkswagen maintained its automotive division net cash flow guidance of €3B to €6B.

The lowered outlook comes as the world’s second-largest automaker faces significant job cuts, intense competition from Chinese rivals in its key European market, and push-back from labor unions who have blocked plans to shutter underperforming plants. Against this backdrop, Volkswagen
to cut its financial and/or sales guidance 4 times since the beginning of 2025.

title: Volkswagen slashes profit guidance as China, restructuring charges, BEV adoption weighs
